findings.title: Ph outside the configured safe range
findings.observed: 2 of 6 readings breached 6.5–8.5 pH units; observed 6.10–7.20 pH units.
findings.expected: Every valid ph reading should remain between 6.5 and 8.5 pH units for this demonstration profile.
findings.detection_logic: A deterministic limit check compared every parsed reading with the documented operating envelope.
findings.why_it_matters: A sustained excursion can indicate sensor error, treatment instability, or a condition requiring independent sampling.
findings.evidence: 2 of 6 readings breached 6.5–8.5 pH units; observed 6.10–7.20 pH units.
findings.recommendation: Verify calibration, obtain an independent sample, inspect the relevant treatment stage, and follow the approved escalation procedure.

findings.title: Unauthorized chemical-dosing activity correlated
findings.observed: 2 non-hold dosing command(s) were explicitly marked unauthorized in the evidence.
findings.expected: Chemical-dosing changes must originate from an approved OT workflow and carry valid authorization context.
findings.detection_logic: The correlation engine joined command intent and authorization state record by record, then checked quality context.
findings.why_it_matters: Unauthorized dosing can create a cyber-physical public-health consequence rather than a network-only alert.
findings.evidence: 2 non-hold dosing command(s) were explicitly marked unauthorized in the evidence.
findings.recommendation: Isolate the command path, preserve logs, independently verify water quality, and restore a validated controller configuration under operator authority.
